analysis: Increasing training negatives from 32 to 128 succeeded in this trial: pinned-host macro validation HR@10 rose from 0.5138 to 0.5262 (+0.0124 absolute). Electronics improved from 0.4200 to 0.4350. Current category HR@10 values were Movies_and_TV 0.5700, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.5400, Electronics 0.4350, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.5600; prior values for the other categories were not supplied, so their individual changes cannot be established. Macro HR@20 increased from 0.6600 to 0.6625. The trial consumed 497.83 allocated GPU-seconds. Results support retaining 128 negatives, but one seeded comparison does not establish generalization or prove that insufficient negatives caused the earlier limitation. No test metrics were available.
code_summary: The sole experimental change was NEGATIVES=128, yielding 129-class sampled-softmax training with the positive at class zero. Negatives remain uniformly sampled, exclude the user's full training history, allow duplicates, and are shared across supervised positions. Each category independently trains one ConvRec: 96-dimensional item embeddings, eight causal residual convolution blocks with dilations [1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8], two-head causal attention with jointly learned relative-distance bias, layer normalization, dropout, and jointly learned item bias. Training retains AdamW, cosine learning-rate decay, seed 42, and validation checkpoint selection. Prediction routes each dataset to exactly one selected checkpoint with matching neural scoring; no ensemble or separately fitted scores are used.
